t.2.92.1: Having settled the army in camp, the mighty Bharata, foremost among those who walk, wished to approach Kākutstha on foot, him who was obedient to his elders.
t.2.92.2: As soon as the army had encamped, each in its appointed place, as if well disciplined, Bharata spoke these words to his brother Śatrughna.
t.2.92.4: As long as I do not see Rāma, or the mighty Lakṣmaṇa, or the illustrious Vaidehī, there will be no peace for me.
t.2.92.3: O gentle one, you should quickly search this forest on every side with bands of men, together with these hunters.
t.2.92.5: Until I behold my brother's auspicious face, radiant like the moon, with eyes like lotus petals, there will be no peace for me.
t.2.92.6: Until I bear upon my head my brother's feet, which carry the marks of a king, I shall have no peace.
t.2.92.7: So long as he who is worthy of the kingdom is not established in the kingdom of his fathers and forefathers, drenched with the waters of consecration, there will be no peace for me.
t.2.92.9: Fortunate is that mountain Citrakūṭa, equal to the king of mountains, on which Kākutstha dwells like Kubera in the Nandana grove.
t.2.92.8: Vaidehī, the illustrious daughter of Janaka, has fulfilled her purpose, she who follows her husband, the lord of the earth that is bounded by the ocean.
t.2.92.11: Having spoken thus, the greatly radiant Bharata, bull among men, that one of great splendor, entered the great forest on foot alone.
t.2.92.10: This impassable forest, haunted by beasts of prey, has fulfilled its purpose, since the greatly splendid Rāma, best of weapon-bearers, dwells in it.
t.2.92.12: He, the best of speakers, went through the midst of those clusters of trees that had grown upon the mountain slopes, their tops covered in blossoms.
t.2.92.13: Having reached a flowering sāla tree on Mount Citrakūṭa, he saw the smoke-banner rising high from the fire in Rāma's hermitage.
t.2.92.14: Seeing it, the glorious Bharata rejoiced together with his kinsmen, and knowing that Rāma was there, he was like one who has reached the far shore of the waters.
t.2.92.15: Having perceived Rāma's hermitage on Mount Citrakūṭa, inhabited by holy people, the great-souled one first encamped the army once more and then went in haste together with Guha.
